doc.title: Bill Mays interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 5, 2025

title: Soundscape release, selling CDs and streaming house concerts
summary: He discusses selling his new CD, streaming, and plans for house concerts.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: Yeah. More good advice. Well this has been a fascinating conversation. I want to congratulate you on your latest recording, it’s called “Soundscape” is that correct?
Yeah. And you’ll be promoting that on gigs I assume?

Yes. I’ll be selling it on gigs. Nobody buys CDs anymore because they don’t have CD players. And it’s available, or will be soon I guess, on Band Camp and places like that. But that’s a whole other thing about the music business, you know where are we going with so many folks being used to downloading music, streaming music. And so many people becoming used to getting stuff for free. You know, why should I plunk down 15 dollars if I can hear his album on this platform or another one. I’m a big believer in the streaming house concert. And I think that Covid brought that to the fore and people

learned that they could get a couple of good cameras and mics and do a very nice production from their music room, something I’m thinking of doing in the new year, maybe doing an every other month concert from the music room and people can donate what they’d like and we’ll see what happens.
